recentItems.title: Houthis claim major advance on Red Sea coast | BBC News
recentItems.description:
Tit-for-tat strikes have continued in Yemen between the Iranian-backed Houthi rebels and pro-government forces aligned to Saudi Arabia. 
 
It comes after a series of military advances by the Houthis, which threaten Saudi oil production. 
 
Those significant territorial gains along the western coast in recent days, including taking Perim Island, a key strategic point next to the Bab al-Mandab Strait, could give the Houthis a possible stronger hold over the strategic waterway.

MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights | BBC News
recentItems.description:
A cross-party group of MPs and peers has identified human rights risks posed by artificial intelligence (AI) which existing laws, they argue, are ill-equipped to cover.
 
The Joint Committee on Human Rights published a report calling for a new bill on AI to "address the scale and seriousness" of such threats.
 
"Nowhere in the world, including the UK, has a current legislative and regulatory approach to AI that is fit for purpose," said Labour MP and committee chair Alex Sobel.

recentItems.title: Linkin Park’s Joe Hahn: Why acknowledging the criticism was essential | BBC News
recentItems.description:
After Chester Bennington's death in 2017, Linkin Park went on an indefinite hiatus. In 2024, the band returned with new music and a new co-vocalist, Emily Armstrong.
 
But what happened behind closed doors during the years in between? In their new documentary film Unshatter, Linkin Park share the process of deciding to make music together again.
 
BBC News' Mel Ramsay speaks with band member and Unshatter director Joe Hahn about navigating grief as well as dealing with criticism - and why the band felt ready to return.

recentItems.title: The billionaires who bankrolled Epstein | BBC News
recentItems.description:
It’s a sex abuse scandal that has gripped the world. But despite all the headlines and stories, important questions remain unanswered about Jeffrey Epstein. 
 
How did he become so powerful? How did he befriend so many important people? And where did the money come from that allowed him to abuse hundreds of girls and young women?
 
Panorama follows the crooked money trail to show how Epstein conned and ingratiated his way into the lives of the super-rich and then used their money to fund his global sex trafficking operation.

recentItems.title: Russia hits train in Ukraine after Boris Johnson, top European officials leave station | BBC News
recentItems.description:
A Russian drone has hit a train near the Ukraine-Poland border shortly after former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson and top European security officials had passed through.
 
No casualties were reported after the strike at Yahodyn, which hit the train's engine. All the passengers had been evacuated, Ukrainian authorities said.
 
Johnson and other European national security advisers, including the UK's Jonathan Powell, had passed along the same line on a different train on their way back from a conference in Kyiv.
 
Russia said it had struck "railway infrastructure" in western Ukraine, but Ukraine's state railway company Ukrzaliznytsia said that "quite possibly, the target of this drone could have been the diplomatic train".

recentItems.title: Donald Trump dismisses AI warnings saying his goal is beating China
recentItems.description:
Donald Trump has brushed aside  the risks posed by artificial intelligence following days of dire warnings by experts.

"You have a lot of very negative forces that are bringing it up that shouldn't be bringing it up and they're bringing up things that won't happen," Trump said during a visit to Ireland.

One of the warnings came from a former Anthropic researcher who said "there is a strong chance that we could all die in the immediate future" if the current pace of development continued.

Some of the AI industry's biggest companies agreed, with their bosses supporting a slow-down. Trump did not directly address the idea, but said: "We're leading China on AI... and, frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins."

Trump spoke on the same day AI researcher Jacob Coxon - who quit Anthropic a few days ago - told the BBC that staff who were developing the systems were "genuinely frightened" for the future of humanity.

Coxon – who has also worked at OpenAI – welcomed the idea of a slowdown but said it would need to be co-ordinated with China.

On Saturday, Elon Musk, owner of xAI, and Sam Altman of OpenAI, backed a warning from the head of Anthropic, Dario Amodei, that the pace of development must be slowed "to reduce the risk that something goes seriously wrong".

Jane Hill presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Ben King and Simon Jack.

recentItems.title: Will Reform have to give their mega donations back? | BBC Newscast
recentItems.description:
After Reform’s £72 million record donations, we’re looking at whether they’ll be allowed to keep the money.

Legislation is going through Parliament that could limit the amount of money foreign donors can give, and be applied restrospectively, but Robert Jenrick has said the recent donations were "entirely in line with the law".

And there’s been a shift in tone from tech bosses since the concerns about AI raised by researchers this week. We look at what a more controlled future for AI might look like.

recentItems.title: Donald Trump says Northern Ireland joining Ireland only natural | BBC News
recentItems.description:
US President Donald Trump has doubled down on his support for a united Ireland.
 
He's on day two of a visit, which he is spending at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg, County Clare, for the Irish Open.
 
On Saturday, Trump told reporters he would love to see a united Ireland while at a meeting with the Taoiseach (Irish PM) Micheál Martin in Dublin.
 
Speaking on Sunday at his Doonbeg golf resort, he said it would be natural to put Ireland and Northern Ireland "together".
 
He spoke to reporters after watching the tournament leader Irish golfer Shane Lowry tee off.
